line: d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 g3 Bg7 Bg2 O-O O-O d5
teaches: When a setup gives you a free choice of central pawn move, pick the one that takes squares away from the opponent rather than the one that only makes room for you — a pawn on the fourth rank of the centre contests two squares at once, usually the two the other side wanted.
explains: Both sides have finished the same quiet development, and this is the move that decides which game gets played. The pawn arriving on d5 covers c4 and e4 together, so the natural pawn breaks are answered before they are even played. The modest alternative one square shorter leaves both of those squares free and invites a bigger centre instead.
